Audit the categorical columns of a data frame for coding hazards

Source: R/categorical_guard.R
audcats.Rd

Checks every categorical column of a data frame for the coding problems that silently change results: numbers that are really category codes whose labels were lost, labels still in foreign value-label form, labels that differ only by case or by an invisible space, empty strings or "NA" stored as a category, unused levels, and identifiers mistaken for categories. Run it once after every import, before any model. It also reports which level R will use as the reference category.

Usage

audcats(data, cols = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

cols

Character vector of column names to audit, default NULL: every factor, character or haven-labelled column. Columns of other types can be named explicitly and are audited by their distinct values.

Value

A data frame of class c("bricklayer_category_audit", "data.frame"), one row per audited column, with character columns column, storage (the column's class), levels (up to eight levels joined with "|"), reference (the first level) and hazards (all hazards joined with " ;; ", or ""), and integer n_levels. The attribute clean is TRUE when no hazard was found. The print method lists each column and its hazards.

Details

For each column the levels are levels(x) for a factor and the sorted distinct values (radix sort, as factor() would order them) otherwise. A hazard is reported when:

  • the column is haven labelled (it still carries value labels and must be decoded with deccodes or declbld);

  • every level looks like a number (^[0-9.]+$);

  • every level starts with a code prefix such as "1. White";

  • a level has leading or trailing whitespace, including non-breaking and other Unicode spaces, or two levels are equal once trimmed;

  • a level is empty, or is a missing-value sentinel (NA, N/A, NAN, NULL, NONE, ., -, ?, compared case-insensitively);

  • the reference (first) level is empty, a sentinel, or padded;

  • two different trimmed levels agree once lower-cased;

  • a factor has levels that never occur;

  • there are more than 50 levels.

The function only reports; it never changes data. It errors when data is not a data frame.

See also

deccodes, grdlvls, xfrvrf.

Examples

# codes without labels, and a case-variant city name
a <- audcats(data.frame(
  race = factor(c("1", "2", "2", "3")),
  city = c("Toronto", "toronto", "Ottawa")[c(1, 2, 3, 3)]
))
a
#> Categorical audit: 2 column(s)
#>   race             factor     3 level(s), reference ‘1’
#>     !! HAZARD: all labels numeric-looking (1,2,3...): likely imported CODES whose value labels were lost; as.numeric() on this column returns level INDICES, not data 
#>   city             character  3 level(s), reference ‘Ottawa’
#>     !! HAZARD: case-variant duplicate labels: ‘Toronto’, ‘toronto’ 
attr(a, "clean")
#> [1] FALSE

# padded, empty and sentinel labels, and an unused level
audcats(data.frame(
  g = factor(c(" A", "A", "NA", ""), levels = c("", " A", "A", "NA", "B"))
))
#> Categorical audit: 1 column(s)
#>   g                factor     5 level(s), reference ‘’
#>     !! HAZARD: labels with leading/trailing whitespace (incl. non-breaking): ‘ A’: a space splits one category into two 
#>     !! HAZARD: whitespace-variant duplicate labels: ‘ A’, ‘A’ 
#>     !! HAZARD: empty-string label "": missingness stored as a category 
#>     !! HAZARD: missing-value sentinel stored as a label: ‘NA’ 
#>     !! HAZARD: the REFERENCE level ‘’ is empty, a sentinel, or differs from a real label only by invisible characters: every model on this column is baselined on it 
#>     !! HAZARD: unused levels: ‘B’ 

# a clean frame; non-categorical columns are skipped by default
audcats(data.frame(sex = c("F", "M", "F"), age = c(31, 45, 27)))
#> Categorical audit: 1 column(s)
#>   sex              character  2 level(s), reference ‘F’
#>   no hazards detected

try(audcats(1:3))
#> Error : audcats: `data` must be a data frame
